messages:
Amy (sales): Heads-up — NovaHealth POC kicks off Mon. They want Redwood Private behind their TGW. Main asks: which topology do we recommend (VPC peering vs PrivateLink) if they need to preserve client source IPs and also have TLS inspection in their DMZ? Also they asked for a ballpark on PrivateLink pricing vs peering for ~5TB/mo.

Devon (eng): Short version: PrivateLink = better isolation + no route exchange. VPC peering = simpler and cheaper for high throughput but requires route sharing and can complicate scoped firewall rules. Preserve-srcip is easiest with peering (no NAT), but you can preserve client IP with PrivateLink only if you terminate TLS on the customer's side (we terminate inside our private deployment so client IP is NATed to endpoint ENI).

Maria (netops): Quick topology sketches:
- Option A (Peering): onprem -> TGW -> spoke VPC -> peering -> redwood-private-vpc -> app ENI (client srcIP preserved)
- Option B (PrivateLink): onprem -> TGW -> spoke -> interface endpoint -> redwood-service-eni (we NAT to endpoint IP)

Maria (netops): ASCII diagram:
```
OnPrem --[TGW/spoke]--> Customer-Spoke-VPC -- Peering --> Redwood-VPC --> App ENI
OnPrem --[TGW/spoke]--> Customer-Spoke-VPC -- Interface Endpoint --> AWS ENI (PrivateLink) --> Redwood
```

Maria (netops): Firewall implications: with peering you allow CIDR ranges between VPCs and preserve client IPs. With PrivateLink you must allow the interface endpoint subnets (ENIs) and expect source to be endpoint IPs. If they have inline TLS inspect, PrivateLink will break end-to-end TLS unless they terminate at their proxy then re-TLS to us.

Amy (sales): They specifically said they need SNI visible to their TLS inspector (so they can block/allow routes). Is that possible with PrivateLink?

Devon (eng): Not without terminating TLS at the customer side. PrivateLink terminates at the endpoint and forwards over our internal path; SNI upstream to their inspector depends on where TLS is terminated. If they need SNI to their DMZ, peering + no NAT is the path.

Paul (security): From a security questionnaire POV: items to call out: mutual TLS support to customer-managed CAs, KMS integration for key material, mTLS enforcement on our side, per-request audit logging (we can export to their SIEM via syslog or S3), and network ACLs for least privilege. We can provide standard attestations for TLS 1.2+, cipher suites, and we support client cert rotation.

Paul (security): Sample firewall snippet customer-side (suggested allowlist):
```
# Customer outbound to Redwood
Allow TCP/443 -> 10.12.34.0/26  # interface endpoint ENIs (PrivateLink)
Allow TCP/443 -> 10.200.0.0/24  # peering CIDR when using peering
# Enforce TLS 1.2+, deny older ciphers
```

Amy (sales): Pricing question — they want a quick delta: for 5TB/mo which is cheaper? They asked for an estimate to include in the SOW.

Devon (eng): Ballpark (very rough): PrivateLink = endpoint hourly + interface data processing + normal data transfer. Example: endpoint ~$0.01/hr (~$7/mo), data processing ~$0.01/GB => for 5TB (~5120GB) that's ~$51 + endpoint hours negligible => ~ $60/mo in infra fees (this excludes cloud provider egress costs). Peering: no endpoint hourly or data-processing surcharge but you'll pay typical cross-AZ/VPC data costs; could be ~ $0.005–0.02/GB depending on region, so for 5TB maybe $25–$100. Net: similar order; peering often cheaper at scale but requires more network ops.

Maria (netops): Also call out support cost: PrivateLink easier for onboarding (no routes to manage) and fits enterprise security teams that forbid cross-account route exchange. If they require deterministic client-ip for logging we should recommend peering or an in-proxy that re-inserts X-Forwarded-For when using PrivateLink.

Amy (sales): Customer also has a security Q on key rotation cadence and whether we store any customer keys. Paul, can you respond to the questionnaire item about KMS/HSM?

Paul (security): We can say: Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations; we do not retain plaintext customer keys. Key rotation supported; we log key usage and can provide audit exports. I'll paste exact wording for their questionnaire to avoid back-and-forth.

Paul (security): Suggested wording (copy-paste safe):
```
Redwood Private: supports integration with customer-managed KMS and HSMs. Customer keys are not exported or stored in plaintext. Key usage is logged (audit events) and exportable for compliance. Key rotation policies and tooling can be coordinated during deployment.
```

Amy (sales): Great. Any enterprise blockers we should flag before sending SOW?

Devon (eng): Potential blockers: 1) If they insist on end-to-end TLS inspected by their DMZ while also requiring preserved client src IP with PrivateLink — that's a topology mismatch. 2) Gov/reg compliance requiring air-gapped deployment — may require Private on-prem package and longer lead time. 3) Network team unwilling to open endpoint ENI CIDRs.

Maria (netops): Ops checklist for handoff to NetOps:
- Preferred topology (peering vs PrivateLink)
- Required client-ip preservation? (yes/no)
- List of allowed outbound CIDRs and ports
- TLS termination point and whether SNI must be visible to their TLS inspector
- Expected throughput (p95 latency/SLA)

Amy (sales): I'll capture that and confirm with NovaHealth. Can someone create a short runbook and the cost delta table I can drop in the SOW? :pray:

deploy-bot: Created ticket RW-3842: "NovaHealth POC — network handoff + cost delta" and linked to runbook draft.

Devon (eng): I'll draft the runbook and the cost table today and drop in RW-3842. Will include both topologies, firewall snippets, and the exact wording for security Qs.

Amy (sales): Thanks all — looping NovaHealth in after I confirm topology choice. :thumbsup:
